newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - March 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - March 2.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company SUNDAY
TELEGRAPH
-- US BANK WILL SUSPEND ROGUE TRADER

Kyriacous Papouis, the chief derivatives trader blamed for a 50 million stg hole in the options trading book at NatWest Markets, the banking arm of National Westminster Bank, is to be suspended by his new employers Bear Stearns, the US securities firm. The Bank of England and the SFA are poised to launch a joint inquiry into the affair.
-- MERRILL PLANS 160 MILLION STG CITY HEADQUARTERS

US investment bank, Merrill Lynch, is preparing to spend more than 160 million stg on a new head office on the site of the old Post Office headquarters in the City of London. The move will tie the American bank to the Square Mile for the long term.
The commitment to the City will be hailed as an important victory by the Corporation of London.
-- RONSON MOVES INTO HIGH STREET

Property magnate Gerald Ronson is planning to move into the high street by building a chain of 250 convenience stores over the next five years. These are to be based on the Snax 24 concept in his service stations. Ronson said he will shortly test the market with three pilot schemes.
-- BABCOCK SET FOR 50 MILLION STG DISPOSAL

Engineering group, Babcock International, is planning a major reorganisation, which includes a series of disposal and joint ventures. The moves will allow the group to quit large-scale contracting, which caused it to suffer a series of losses and provisions in the past. The group is concentrating on its smaller business.
-- CHURCH HIT FOR ONE MILLION STG BY PACE PRICE COLLAPSE

The Church of England has lost one million stg by backing Pace Micro Technology, the digital television group whose shares crashed last week. The Church Commissioners lost half the value of their holding in Pace and a spokesman said that it is impossible to say if the investment has been lost because the shares have not yet been sold.
SUNDAY TIMES
-- SFO TO LAUNCH PROBE AT NATWEST

The Serious Fraud Office is to launch an investigation into the 50 million stg of losses in the derivatives-trading arm of NatWest Group. The bank suspended Neil Dodgson, the manager responsible for fixed-interest options, after the discovery of losses due to "mispricing errors" at NatWest Markets.
-- ROBINSON: WHY I AM DITCHING MAJOR FOR BLAIR

Chairman of Granada, Gerry Robinson is the latest top business figure to declare support for Labour Party leader Tony Blair. This will provide a further boost to Labour in its campaign to forge links with the business community. Robinson said his move coincided with his disillusionment with John Major.
-- CHINESE PUSH FOR A DEAL WITH CABLE AND WIRELESS

Cable and Wireless is facing pressure from Beijing to admit rivals into the territory's dominant telecoms operator and cut its 59 percent stake in Hongkong Telecom to less than 50 percent. According to insiders China is prepared to hand C&W a stake in the mainland Chinese telephone market, which has already been imposed on other Hong Kong businesses.
-- CLARKE CHALLENGES CRITICS OVER BUDGET DEFICIT AND BASE RATE

Chancellor Kenneth Clarke is to admit that public finances are improving faster than he expected in the budget and that consumers remain sensitive to price rises, which is helping to maintain low inflation. Officials see this period as an important mid-term assessment. Clarke is to claim that attitudes to inflation in Britain have changed, helped by the "transparency" of the monetary-policy arrangements in place for the past four years.
-- HAMBROS TO TEAM UP WITH GUINNESS FLIGHT

Hambros and Guinness Mahon, the investment banks, are to unveil a merger of their fund-management arms to create a business with seven billion stg assets under management. Hambros Fund Management will merge with Guinness Flight, Guinness Mahon's 64 percent-owned offshoot, to form Guinness Flight Hambros.
THE OBSERVER
-- BALLS SET FOR KEY TREASURY JOB

Economic adviser to shadow chancellor Gordon Brown, Ed Balls, is set to head the Treasury's new policy unit if the Labour Party win the general election. He will become the youngest manager of the UK economy for decades whilst remaining Brown's leading aide.
-- 'UNHAPPY' FORMER KLEINWORT HEAD SET TO COLLECT A MILLION

Former chairman of merchant bank Kleinwort Benson, Simon Robertson, is set to receive a seven-figure compensation package, which could be close to one million stg. He resigned over "irreconcilable differences" with German parent Dresdner.
It is thought Robertson will find a new job quickly.
-- ROGUE FUND MANAGER MAY BE UNFIT TO STAND TRAIL

Rogue fund manager Peter Young could escape prosecution after he declared himself mentally and legally incompetent to defend a civil action brought against him by the bank. He may also be considered unfit to face any criminal prosecution by the Serious Fraud Office.
-- SMART MONEY GOES ON LADBROKE CASINO BIDS
Ladbroke, the leisure group, is tipped to step into the battle between London Clubs and Capital Corporation for control of two of Britain's casinos, Crockfords and the Colony Club.
There is speculation that Ladbroke may try to tie up with London Clubs. Ladbroke, however, refused to comment.
-- INVESTORS TO SUE OVER $20 MILLION FRAUD

Investors are planning to sue Thompson Trading, part of the private business empire controlled by David Thompson, for compensation after losing more than $20 million in a series of inter-related frauds. This follows the jailing of German business agent Nicolas Gross over a related fraud. Thompson Trading maintains it was duped by Gross.
- - - - INDEPENDENT ON SUNDAY
-- FUND CHIEF UNDER SCRUTINY

Stephen Bamford, former head of US insurer Metropolitan Life's international investment arm and who is under scrutiny following the Deutsche Morgan Grenfell/Peter Young affair, has emerged as key backer of Alpha Omikron, an AIM company, which features in one of Britain's biggest ever insider-dealing inquiries. He also brokered a deal which left Alpha with one of MetLife's loss-making investments, Medical Underwriting Services Ltd, a medical information company.
-- AVIS INC IN $1 BILLION FLOAT

US car rental business, Avis Incorporated, is preparing to join Avis Europe and rival Hertz with a stock market listing which will value the company at around $1 billion. US hotel to property group which owns Avis Inc, HFS, is preparing to accelerate plans to float off the business in order to capitalise on new investment interest in the car retail sector.
-- ALLIED DOMECQ TO SHED 700 JOBS

Allied Domecq has launched a streamlining of its worldwide accounting and finance operations, which could lead to 700 job losses and save 15 million stg a year. The Financial Process Redesign Project is being put together by Allied's director of taxation, Peter Lyster, and is intended to shorten communication lines and improve the quality of information available to management.
-- RANGERS BACKER SEEKS A STAKE IN EUROPEAN ELITE

Billionaire Joe Lewis, who was recently paid 40 million stg for a 25 percent stake in Glasgow Rangers football club, is to create an investment portfolio of European football clubs. This comes at a time when outside investors are buying a lot of stakes in top European clubs, many of which are preparing to float.
-- NEW PEARSON BOSS PLANS ONE BILLION STG SELL-OFFS

Marjorie Scardino, new chief executive of media and leisure group Pearson, is planning one billion stg worth of sell-offs. The City expects stakes in BSkyB and Lazards to go, as well as loss-making US multi-media firm Mindscape and the disposal or demerger of Tussauds leisure. This follows a 100 million stg loss from an accounting fraud at Penguin books in the US.
MAIL ON SUNDAY
-- UNILEVER CHIEF HITS AT THE 'SMUG' CITY

Niall FitzGerald, chairman of Unilever, has launched an attack on the City of London, with accusations of smugness. He says that many fund managers do not earn their huge salaries and London is being overtaken by New York and faces being left behind in Europe. He stresses that he speaks as an industrialist rather than an expert.
-- FA PLAYS INVESTORS ON-SIDE

The Football Association is planning to relax rules banning an investor from owning a sizeable stake in more than one club. This comes as Tony Berry, a Spurs director and former Blue Arrow chairman, attempts to buy Millwall Football Club. The FA hopes that talks with the DTI will lead to a higher limit before its annual meeting in June.
-- LITTLEWOODS MAY LINK WITH ASDA

Littlewoods is in talks with Asda, the superstores group, about co-operating over their clothing business. Archie Norman, Asda ASDD.L chairman, has declared his intention of making Asda into the second largest family clothing retailer in Britain after Marks and Spencer. Littlewoods is looking at ways to increase profitability of its High Street department stores.
-- DEFIANT GRAN FIGHTS GIANT CORPORATION

Eileen Burnett is rallying support to take on Anglo-America Corporation in a patent dispute. She runs a small electronics business, which has been accused by Anglo-American of patent infringement. Electronics giants, such as Siemens and Texas Instruments, are backing Burnett because if she losses Anglo- American will use the victory to demand royalty payments from them.
-- 'LURE FIRMS TO UK WITH WINDFALL TAX'

Bosses of privatised utilities, such as SWEB, United Utilities and Yorkshire Electricity, are pressing the Labour Party to use a windfall profit tax to stimulate foreign investment. They are resigned to paying the tax if Labour wins the general election, but want it invested in regional infrastructure projects that will attract overseas companies.
